title.narrative: Support to Emergency Response Rooms Providing Hot Meals in Khartoum and Jebal Awlia

description.narrative: In the face of a worsening food crisis driven by conflict, WFP has forged critical partnerships with community-based organizations to reach areas cut off from traditional food assistance and cash transfers. In RSF and SAF controlled zones of Khartoum, WFP supports a lifesaving initiative of community kitchens and Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs), directly confronting the escalating hunger crisis by delivering hot meals through 200 kitchens using an indirect cash-transfer system. Originally planned in June 2024 to serve 96,000 people monthly, the initiative already exceeded the expectations. By August 2024, the hot meals were reaching 292,000 people daily, and an additional 235,000 were served in September alone. Targeting severely affected areas like Sheriq Al Nil, Jebel Awlia, Khartoum, and Bahri—all classified as IPC4 and IPC5, indicating extreme food insecurity, this program is a lifeline for the people of Khartoum. These numbers could fluctuate due to the increased level of violence in the area. In targeted risk of famine localities, in Khartoum and Jebel Awlia, meals provide 1,457 kilocalories, meeting 70 percent of daily nutritional needs. Access is universal and does not require beneficiary registration, nor ration cards. With security risks and movement restrictions, anyone in need can receive meals, ensuring rapid and inclusive support. A key challenge remains the lack of qualified financial service providers in these areas, prompting WFP to rely on trusted local NGOs to manage funds and oversee meal distribution. After two implementation cycles, WFP has evaluated these partnerships and is considering scaling up the initiative to reach even more people in desperate need. In a region where traditional food distribution is nearly impossible due to conflict, this initiative is a vital lifeline. Even amidst chaos, with every hot meal, WFP and its partners deliver lifesaving support reaching those who need it most.
